claims.text: Large language models are prone to generating hallucinations, which are plausible but factually incorrect responses.
Large language models express hallucinations with striking confidence.
Hallucinations and non-factual responses generated by LLMs can be detected by examining the model's uncertainty in its response.
Uncertainty quantification methods for LLMs can be applied to chatbot and textual applications.
Uncertainty quantification methods for LLMs can be applied to embodied artificial intelligence applications in robotics.

evidence.description: given their propensity to generate hallucinations: plausible, factually-incorrect responses
which are expressed with striking confidence.
Previous work has shown that hallucinations and other non-factual responses generated by LLMs can be detected by examining the uncertainty of the LLM in its response to the pertinent prompt
highlight applications of uncertainty quantification methods for LLMs, spanning chatbot and textual applications
to embodied artificial intelligence applications in robotics.

methodologies.name: LLM Uncertainty Quantification Taxonomy
methodologies.description: A taxonomy and survey framework unifying disparate uncertainty quantification methods for large language models.

limitations.text: LLMs tend to generate hallucinations and non-factual responses expressed with high confidence, raising concerns regarding their reliability and trustworthiness.

future_work.text: Addressing open research challenges in the uncertainty quantification of LLMs.
